detailed_rationale:
KSB Limited is the Indian listed arm of the German KSB SE group, manufacturing pumps and valves for power (including nuclear), petrochemical, water/infrastructure, metro-rail and general industrial applications. The quant data for this stock is almost entirely blank (market cap, ROE, ROCE, D/E, interest coverage, revenue CAGR, and the quality/growth/value scores are all missing, and the model's own zero_cov_flag is set True), which reflects a data-pipeline gap for this name rather than an absence of real, findable fundamentals -- my own web research surfaced usable figures the quant feed evidently did not capture. Standalone results for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (Q4 FY26, board-approved April 30, 2026) showed revenue of Rs 601.3 crore (Pumps Rs 499.5 crore, Valves Rs 102.5 crore) and standalone profit of Rs 37.3 crore (consolidated Rs 39.8 crore, EPS Rs 2.28). As of December 2025 the company carried a total order book of Rs 2,585 crore, roughly half of it nuclear-sector orders -- a specialized, high-barrier-to-entry segment that is a genuine long-cycle revenue-visibility positive, alongside strength in power, petrochemical, metro and water-sector orders per the company's own Q1 FY26 commentary (which also noted lower PBT that quarter despite strong order wins, suggesting some near-term margin/execution lag versus the order pipeline).

Given the scale of the quant model's data gap for this name, I am flagging this explicitly as a methodology issue rather than treating the blank fields as neutral: a NSE-listed, disclosure-compliant industrial company with real quarterly financials and a substantial, diversified order book should not be showing zero coverage in a fundamentals-driven scoring model, and this may point to a broader data-pipeline gap affecting other thinly-covered small/micro-cap names in the 750-universe, not just KSB.
recommendation_rationale: Quant composite is Hold (on the limited scoring the model could compute), and my own research -- while more limited than for a fully-covered stock -- did not surface any distress signal: the company is profitable, order-book diversified (nuclear/power/petrochemical/metro/water), and part of a global engineering group. Given the real data gap here, I am keeping Hold rather than asserting a confident independent view either way, and flagging the coverage gap itself for the data/quant team.
summary: KSB Limited makes industrial pumps and valves, including specialized equipment for nuclear power plants, and is the Indian arm of a German engineering group. The standard scoring data for this stock was almost entirely missing, but our own research found a profitable company with a healthy, diversified order book spanning power, nuclear, petrochemical, metro and water projects. We rate it a Hold based on what we could verify, while flagging that the underlying data coverage for this stock needs to be fixed.
positive_para: A diversified order book of Rs 2,585 crore as of December 2025, roughly half from nuclear-sector projects, gives long-cycle revenue visibility in a specialized segment with high barriers to entry that few Indian pump/valve makers can access. Being part of the global KSB SE group provides access to engineering know-how and a customer base spanning power, petrochemical, metro-rail and water infrastructure -- all areas of sustained Indian capex.
negative_para: The scoring data available for this stock is almost entirely missing (market cap, leverage, return ratios, growth rates and the composite quality/growth/value scores are all blank), which means this Hold call rests on a thinner independent verification base than most other names in this batch; company commentary itself has flagged lower profit before tax in at least one recent quarter despite strong order wins, suggesting some near-term execution or margin lag versus the headline order-book strength that is worth monitoring once fuller data is available.
reverse_dcf_judgment: Without reliable ROE/ROCE/leverage data from the quant feed, a full reverse-DCF read is not responsible here; based on the standalone quarterly profit (Rs 37.3 crore on Rs 601.3 crore revenue, an ~6% net margin) and a healthy, diversified order book, the business appears to be a steady, moderately profitable industrial franchise rather than either a distressed name or an obvious re-rating candidate. This judgment should be revisited once proper fundamental coverage is restored.
